target_query: what is the difference between larger smaller and size in gmail search

drafted_by.identity: Claude Opus 5.5 scheduled editorial draft job (Claude Code)

sources.supports: size:, larger: and smaller: share one table row described as 'Find emails by their size' with examples size:1000000 and larger:10M (no smaller: example); number rule that a space or dash separates a number and a dot is a decimal; negative-operator caveat that Gmail 'identifies matching messages first'; page is the Computer version.
sources.review_notes: Fetched 2026-10-20 by the drafting agent (WebFetch and a raw curl text extraction, both agreeing). Confirmed the shared row wording and both examples verbatim. The page does NOT state units beyond the M example, whether thresholds are inclusive, whether M is decimal or binary, whether size: means at-least or exact, whether decimals are accepted, or any sort-by-size option. The draft states each of these as undocumented. Extending the 'matching messages first' caveat from negative operators to size searches is the draft's reasoning, presented as such.

sources.supports: The search options panel has a Size field described as 'Searches for emails that match a certain size'.
sources.review_notes: Fetched 2026-10-20 via curl text extraction. Confirmed the Size field wording. The page gives no detail on its comparison choices or units, and the draft does not claim any; it only suggests comparing the generated query with a typed one. Whether the panel writes a query into the search box was not verified and the FAQ wording should be checked by a reviewer.

sources.supports: Deleted messages go to Trash and are recoverable for 30 days.
sources.review_notes: Relied on the 30-day Trash statement as confirmed in sibling drafts' 2026-10-17 fetch; not re-fetched in this run. Cited only for the cleanup step of the self-test.

sources.supports: Base64 content-transfer-encoding represents each 24-bit group (3 bytes) of input as 4 encoded characters, with encoded lines no longer than 76 characters.
sources.review_notes: Fetched rfc2045.txt 2026-10-20 and located section 6.8 text on 24-bit groups and the 76-character line limit. The draft says only that an encoded attachment is about a third larger; it explicitly says Google does not document whether size search counts encoded or raw bytes.

serp_review.query: gmail search difference between size: larger: smaller: operator
serp_review.observation: Standard web search returned Google's 7190 reference, third-party operator guides (ionos.com, webnots.com, supportbee.com, computerworld.com, a helpdesk page) and a Google Workspace Cloud Search reserved-operators page. Third-party guides commonly assert size: is a bytes-only version of larger: and disagree on whether the boundary is inclusive; none separated Google-documented facts from inference or offered a way to check the thresholds. The Cloud Search page concerns a different product and was not used as evidence (fetch also timed out).
serp_review.limitation: A single standard US search; not a full Google SERP capture. Third-party guide content was seen only through search summaries, not fetched.

information_gain: A documented-versus-undocumented table for the three operators (what Google's single shared row actually says vs. inclusivity, MB definition, units, exact-vs-at-least size:), a job-to-query decision table, and a reader-runnable known-size bracketing test that explains why a message can be larger than its attachment (Base64 per RFC 2045) and lets readers measure where Gmail's thresholds fall. The hub (gmail-delete-emails-by-size) and how-to-find-biggest-emails-gmail give recipes but neither explains how the three operators differ or what is undocumented.
overlap_check: Hub gmail-delete-emails-by-size owns the deletion procedure and how-to-find-biggest-emails-gmail owns the discovery recipe; this draft links to both and does not repeat their steps. Deferred topic gmail-search-operator-size-larger ('search larger than a certain size') is owned by the hub. Pending gmail-large-email-query-no-results (troubleshooting no results) remains distinct: this draft does not troubleshoot empty results. Pending gmail-find-large-emails-without-attachments is only touched in one table row.
limitations: Source and documentation review only; no live Gmail mailbox test was run. The known-size bracketing test is presented as a method for readers with no expected results, and its outcome (encoded vs raw counting, inclusive boundaries, MB definition, K unit, decimals, size: semantics) is unverified.
The step-4 interpretation (matching larger:3M for a file just under 3 MB suggests encoded counting) also depends on Gmail's undocumented M definition; a reviewer may want to soften or test it.
The FAQ about the search-options Size field assumes Gmail shows a generated query in the search box; this was not verified.
The 7401 Trash statement was not re-fetched in this run.
Mobile app operator support is not discussed; the cited reference is the computer version.
review_needed: An independent substantive reviewer should re-read 7190 and 6593 claim by claim, decide whether the step-4 interpretation and the Size-field FAQ need softening or a live test, ideally run the known-size test in a real mailbox (recording assets if so), then record evidence_checked or publish_ready with their real identity, verified_on and post_sha256 in scripts/content-records.json during a separate promotion.
